subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Access, Cost, Facilities, and Community Resources
title: Synthesis and review: community, workplace, and campus activity options under transfer
focus: community, workplace, and campus activity options
essentialQuestion: What does it actually cost to stay active, and what costs nothing?
materials: publicly available facility and program information
privacySafeScenario: Produce an access plan comparing at least three ways to stay active after graduation on different budgets, including one that costs nothing, and identify the failure point of each.
studentTask: Learner works community, workplace, and campus activity options costed against a real budget the learner sets, building an activity life at the lowest workable spend at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of community, workplace, and campus activity options degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds community, workplace, and campus activity options costed against a real budget the learner sets, building an activity life at the lowest workable spend, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: The comparison may be written, tabled, or spoken; publicly available information is supplied if the learner cannot research independently.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of community, workplace, and campus activity options yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The comparison may be written, tabled, or spoken; publicly available information is supplied if the learner cannot research independently.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where community, workplace, and campus activity options shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
